inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: While the Taoiseach claims in Limerick that tenancies have increased due to his government's March 1 rules for six-year leases, he's choosing to ignore the spike in eviction notices and homelessness. At the same time, the numbers of people in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationally. This highlights the deep structural inequalities trapping vulnerable communities in housing insecurity, where even modest reforms get undermined by entrenched power imbalances favoring property owners over people in need. We need far stronger institutional changes to deliver real tenant protections and address the systemic roots of homelessness and instability.
